# v1.1.0-dev.86 — One set of controls for several monitors

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.85`.

## Change Several Displays With One Set Of Controls

dev.85 let you select more than one monitor. What it then showed you was a
stack of identical cards with a small strip above them carrying two of the
settings, which is the same options listed twice.

There is one card now. Scaling, Orientation, Resolution and Refresh rate,
listed once, applying to every display you picked.

### It Only Offers What They Can All Do

Two displays rarely offer the same thing. One panel's scaling ladder might
be 100, 125, 150 while another's is 100, 150, 200. Their resolution lists
are routinely different sizes entirely.

So the shared controls list what every selected display can honour, and
nothing else. Offering everything either of them could do would let you
pick 125% for a pair where one cannot do it. The apply would then half
work without saying anything.

Resolutions are compared long side first. A monitor standing on its end
therefore still matches an upright one of the same shape. Each display
then stores the size from its own list, which keeps a rotated display's saved setting
naming something its driver actually offers.

### And It Says So When They Disagree

Pick two displays running at different scales and the readout says **now
mixed** rather than naming one of them.

Orientation does the same. That one mattered. A landscape display and a
portrait one used to show "Landscape", which was untrue about the second
and would have quietly rotated it the moment you chose a resolution. It
reads **Mixed, leave as they are** now, and only changes anything if you
actually pick something.

## History Is A Dialog

The list of earlier arrangements was a panel wedged into the bottom of the
display editor. It opens as a proper dialog now, the same shape as the
History window for a profile: a heading, a titled list that fills the
window, and its own buttons.

Every row draws the arrangement it describes. A small picture of your desk
as it was, with the primary display picked out. That is what let the
preview mode go away, because you can see which one you want before you
choose it.

Choosing one still draws it in the editor rather than applying it. The
15 second Keep or Revert countdown is exactly where it was.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
